Ever tried to spin up a backend without writing a single line of code?

I recently came across Xano, a visual API builder that lets you design endpoints on top of a PostgreSQL database.

What caught my eye is how quickly you can prototype data models, set up relationships, and expose RESTful APIs without worrying about server configs.

In my own experiments, I connected Xano to a small analytics pipeline and saved days of setup time.

Here are a few things I found useful:

- The drag‑and‑drop interface makes schema changes visible instantly, so you can iterate with the whole team.

- Built‑in authentication and role‑based permissions let you secure APIs without writing auth code.

- You can still run custom SQL queries when you need fine‑grained control, keeping the power of PostgreSQL at your fingertips.

If you’re juggling data pipelines and need a fast way to expose data to front‑end apps, give Xano a try.

Do you think visual API tools will replace traditional backend coding in the next few years?

#NoCode #Backend #APIDevelopment #PostgreSQL

concept_posts.post_content:
Ever tried to connect QuickSight to a data source in a private subnet and hit a wall?

I ran into that last month when I needed to pull data from an RDS instance inside our VPC.

QuickSight can talk to resources in a VPC,
 but only if you set up VPC connectivity correctly.

Think of it like a private tunnel that lets QuickSight’s managed compute nodes reach your databases without exposing them to the internet.

In our case we created a VPC endpoint for QuickSight,
 attached it to the same subnet as the RDS,
 and granted the QuickSight service role permission to the security group.

Key takeaways:

- Use a VPC endpoint or a private link to keep traffic inside AWS.
- Align security groups so that QuickSight’s ENIs are allowed inbound on the DB port.
- Enable encryption in transit for extra safety.

A common mistake is opening the database to 0.0.0.0/0 in the security group,
 thinking it’s easier.

That instantly defeats the purpose of a private VPC.

What’s your go‑to pattern for securing QuickSight connections?
